Project · 03/2026 — present · v1.3.0-rc.3 · Supervised institutional pilot candidate

Face Clock Evoluir

Built for an educational institution: 1:N facial identification, a FastAPI backend, and PostgreSQL/pgvector on CPU-only hardware. Deployed to a test environment; a supervised institutional pilot candidate. Institutional calibration and operational approval remain pending.

See what is pilot-readyInspect the experiments

Problem and constraints

Recognition must work within an operational routine.

The institution needs 1:N facial identification, understandable kiosk feedback, HR review, auditability, and deployment on its CPU-only server.

I developed the models, FastAPI APIs, PostgreSQL/pgvector persistence, tests, interfaces, and test-environment deployment.

Solution

From capture to an auditable record.

  1. 01Capture

    The kiosk guides the employee through the camera and recovery states.

  2. 02Identify

    YuNet and SFace run through OpenCV DNN; pgvector stores embeddings for 1:N search.

  3. 03Record, review, and resolve

    Calendars, hour balances, HR review, and audit trails support exceptions.

Engineering decisions

Measured engineering decisions

Problem → Measurement → Decision → Limitation. Each link opens its protocol.

Threshold for 1:N identification

Inherited 1:1 threshold → 45.4% unknown-person acceptance; at 0.50, 0.2% → recalibrate → enrolled-user rejection and gallery effects need institutional measurement.

See measurement and limit →

Exact or approximate search

1,000 vectors → exact search 0.076 ms; HNSW 0.04 ms, recall@1 0.915 → keep exact pgvector search → the trial does not establish larger-scale performance.

See measurement and limit →

Concurrent extraction

Shared state → two concurrent attendance attempts caused 6/6 failures → serialize access and test eight threads → capacity still depends on server hardware.

See measurement and limit →

CPU latency

Three-frame burst → p95 of 74 ms with one identification and 1.87 s with twenty → size concurrency → controlled benchmark, without institutional operational validation.

See measurement and limit →

Runtime and image size

Heavy inference image → historical change from 8.1 GB to 433 MB, with no changed test decisions → ONNX Runtime → disk, RAM, and multi-stage gains are separate measurements.

See measurement and limit →

Model lineage

Mismatched packaged artifact → checkpoint and ONNX audit → checksums and lineage verified at release → separate from the classifier benchmark.

See measurement and limit →

Inference isolation

OCR dominates processing → 909 ms versus 14 ms for the network → separate triage service → environment-specific cost, without a throughput claim.

See measurement and limit →

The CPU-only target and the delivered package were tested separately from model metrics; see the technical protocols.

Delivery and limits

Pilot candidate, with limits documented.

The project reached v1.3.0-rc.3 after three release candidates, targeted validation, and hands-on deployment in a test environment.

It does not replace a certified REP-P. Calibration with the institution's population and operational approval remain pending.
